title: Build a small unit-converter web tool (length + weight), but he disagrees with the AI's proposed step order ('why styling before the conversion logic?') and challenges a step's rationale — all while running fully in English.
preconditions: David, an English-speaking exchange student and confident beginner. He has the app set to English locale and actively pushes back on the AI when its plan ordering or a step's rationale doesn't match his own (sometimes wrong) intuition.
steps: Design: David runs the Socratic interview in English. He expects every prompt, the PrdAuthoringBoard labels, scope/non-goals, and criteria to render in English — and he expects the AI's replies to be in English, not Korean.

Plan: AI drafts a plan; David disagrees with the ordering and the rationale for one step. He uses the RationaleChallengePanel to push back in English, asking the AI to justify or re-order. He expects a real engagement with his objection (accept / counter / adjust offer), not a rubber-stamp 'you're right' or a stubborn refusal.

Implement: Steps run with English PermissionCards (diff preview, approve/deny). He denies one write with an English reason ('wrong file') and expects the denial + reason to be recorded and the turn to recover gracefully.

Verify: The evidence-gated stepper and any provocation/review cards render in English with criterion-linked questions; he opens the preview and runs the converter. He expects 'change confirmed' / supply-chain tags and all secondary status badges to be English, and the verification card's challenge to be a genuine criterion check.
Done: Converter verified done, checkpoint saved, all in English. He expects a fully English 'done' state with no Korean leaking into badges or labels.
expected: DIVE treats disagreement as a first-class interaction: the RationaleChallengePanel lets him contest the plan and gets a substantive accept/counter/adjust response (the AI defends a good ordering or genuinely revises a weak one), denials are recorded cleanly, and — critically — the ENTIRE experience stays in English: prompts, AI replies, status badges, supply-chain tags, and verification cards, so a non-Korean beginner is never left guessing.
notes: Watch for: This journey directly hits two known defects: (1) DEF-01 — hardcoded-Korean secondary badges/tags (실행 중, 계획 검토 필요, 승인 필요, 변경 확인 필요, AI 자가보고만 있음 from agencyStatus.ts + provocation/product files) leak Korean into his English UI; (2) the LLM tends to reply in Korean even at English locale, so his Socratic interview / rationale-challenge answers may come back in Korean. Also watch: does RationaleChallengePanel give a real counter-argument or just capitulate?; does a denied write recover the turn without dead-ending?
